overlays/context-menu.notes:
Every text, icon, shortcut and colour of the menu comes from your `items` (the `MenuItem` of `Menu`), so there is
nothing built in to replace: `<ContextMenu items={items} menuClass="files-menu" label="File actions">…</ContextMenu>`.
overlays/context-menu.a11y:
The panel is a `menu` of `menuitem`s; the first item takes focus, ↑ ↓ Home End move, Enter runs, Escape closes and
returns focus to where it was. Shift+F10 and the Menu key open it at the focused element, so it never needs a pointer.

overlays/dialog.notes:
```tsx
<Dialog open={$open} onClose={close} title="Invite" closeButton={false} motion="fade">…</Dialog>
<Dialog open={$open} onClose={close} title="Invite" closeButton={arrowLeft} closeLabel="Back to the list">…</Dialog>
```

`openDialog(render, { title, size, footer, dismissable, dismissValue, closeButton, closeLabel, motion })`, `openDrawer(render, { side: "left" | "right" | "bottom", … })`,
`confirm("Delete it?")` or `confirm({ title, message, danger, ok, cancel })` → `boolean`, `prompt({ title, label, value, placeholder, validate, multiline, ok, cancel })` → `string | null`,
`askReason({ title, min, purposes, ok, cancel, labels, counter })` → the text (or `{ category, text }`) or `null`.

Every text of the ready-made dialogs is yours: `ok` and `cancel` name the buttons; `askReason` also takes
`labels: { reason, purpose, choose, choosePurpose, tooShort: (min) => string }` (field labels, the empty choice and the
two error messages) and `counter: false` (no character counter). All three take `dialog: { size, class, target,
closeButton, closeLabel, motion }` for the look of the dialog itself:

```tsx
await prompt({ title: "New name", ok: "Rename", cancel: "Keep the old one", dialog: { motion: "rise", closeButton: false } });
await askReason({ min: 20, counter: false, labels: { reason: "Why?", tooShort: (n) => `At least ${n} characters, please.` } });
```
overlays/dialog.a11y:
`role="dialog"` (alertdialog for confirm), `aria-modal`, labelled by the title. Focus moves into the dialog, Tab stays
inside, Escape closes the topmost one (a popover inside closes first), focus returns to the opener. The page behind
is scroll-locked. On phones the panel rises from the bottom edge; drawers mirror in right-to-left layouts.

`openDrawer()` (and `openDialog(render, { kind: "drawer", side })`) opens the `<Drawer>` component: one drawer, with its
grab handle, drag to close and logical sides. Its module is loaded when the first one opens.

```tsx

<Drawer open={$open} onClose={close} side="end" motion={{ duration: 520, exit: 300, easing: "easeOutBack" }} title="Details">…</Drawer>
```

overlays/drawer.a11y:
`role="dialog"`, labelled by the title (or `label`); `aria-modal` only when modal. Escape closes the topmost one, focus
moves in and returns to the opener. With snap points the grab handle is a button ("Resize panel") that steps through
them with Enter / Space, so every size is reachable without a pointer. With reduced motion the panel appears at once.

Content longer than the sheet scrolls in the body only (`overscroll-behavior: contain`; the modal layer locks the page,
iOS included). At a smaller snap point the body ends at the screen edge, so its last line can be scrolled to. A drag
on the body scrolls it first; at its top, dragging down moves the sheet (and closes it past the smallest point).

overlays/popover.a11y:
The trigger gets `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. The panel is a `dialog` (or the `role` you
give) named by its title or `label`; it is not modal: the page stays reachable. Opening moves focus to the first
control in the panel (or the panel); Escape and the close button return it to the trigger; a press outside closes
without moving focus. Escape is taken before a dialog underneath sees it. The panel lives in the popover layer
(Portal), keeps the theme and colour of its trigger, and shows without animation under reduced motion.

overlays/toast.notes:
```tsx
toast("Level up!", { icon: "🎉", color: "brand-purple", closable: false, motion: "fade", timeout: 3000 });
toast("Saved", { icon: false, closeLabel: "Close the message" });
```

`toast.dismiss(id)`, `toast.clear()`, `toast.list()` (reactive). `<ToastHost />` renders the stack where you place it
(optional); it takes `position` (`bottom-end` default, `bottom-start`, `bottom-center`, `top-end`, `top-start`,
`top-center`; start / end follow the writing direction) and `class`: `<ToastHost position="top-center" />`.
overlays/toast.a11y:
The stack is a polite live region: a new toast is read once (the toasts add no live region of their own); danger
toasts are `role="alert"`. Auto-dismiss timers pause while the pointer or the focus is on the stack. Each has a "Dismiss"
button (translated) and the action button, both reachable with Tab; the toast does not take focus. On narrow screens
the stack spans the width.

props: hover delay before it shows (focus shows it at once)
overlays/tooltip.notes:
```tsx
<Tooltip text="Saved" color="success" delay={0} motion="fade"><IconButton icon={check} label="Save" /></Tooltip>
<Tooltip text="Copy link" disabled={() => $touch}><Button>Share</Button></Tooltip>
```
overlays/tooltip.a11y:
`role="tooltip"` and `aria-describedby` on the wrapped element while shown; keyboard focus shows it, Esc hides it.
It never holds interactive content (use Dropdown for that) and never receives pointer events.
